newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Annan pleased at Cyprus missing persons agreement.
newsitem.headline: Annan pleased at Cyprus missing persons agreement.

text.p: Secretary-General Kofi Annan is pleased with the "unexpectedly positive outcome" of talks in Nicosia between the leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities on the fate of missing persons, U.N. spokesman Fred Eckhard said on Friday.
The two sides agreed, as a first step, to provide each other immediately and simultaneously with information on the location of graves, he said.
The talks, between President Glafcos Clerides and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash, were held under the auspices of the U.N. resident representative in Nicosia, Gustave Feissel.
"The secretary-general is very pleased with the unexpectedly positive outcome of the talks in Nicosia between the leaders of the two Cypriot communities yesterday," Eckhard said.

Annan was "actively considering appointing" a new U.N. member to a committee on missing persons that also includes representatives of the two communities "so that it can get on with its work, now that the two sides have indicated a seriousness in dealing with this issue," Eckhard added.
He said the three-member committee, established in 1981, had become largely inactive and when the previous U.N. representative retired he had not been replaced.

The Greek Cypriots say 1,619 members of their community have been missing since 1974, when Turkish troops occupied the northern third of the island after a coup in Nicosia engineered by the military then ruling Greece.
Turkish Cypriots say 803 of their community are missing after intercommunal clashes dating back to the 1960s.

The talks in Nicosia on humanitarian issues follow meetings between Clerides and Denktash at a rural New York resort from July 9 to 12 aimed at reviving negotiations on reuniting their divided island as a bi-communal, bi-zonal federation. They are expected to hold another round of meetings in Switzerland later this month.
